parents.subject: Natural Resources and Environmental Sciences
parents.course: Adv GIS for Nat Res Planning

ns2:section.sectionText: NRES 455 examines advanced applications of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing for environmental management. This course integrates current geospatial tools and methods to learn applied techniques for collecting spatial data, building spatial models and databases, analyzing spatial patterns, managing environmental issues, and communicating science through interactive mapping applications. Course exercises provide hands-on learning approaches and introduce students to programming principles for GIS. Prerequisite: NRES 454 or GGIS 379. The credit hours for this course will be changed from 2 hours to 3 hours upon university approval. This course will meet in the ACES Library and Alumni Center computer classroom.
